newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU energy taxation proposals will hit gas unfairly.
newsitem.headline: EU energy taxation proposals will hit gas unfairly.

text.p: European proposals to tax gas according to its energy content take no account of its superior environmental friendliness, the executive vice-president of Statoil told the European Gas 97 conference on Tuesday.

"In a political environment where emphasis is put on the environment, the prospects for gas ought to be bright...(but it is) rather the opposite," Peter Mellbye told an audience of gas industry heads.
He said that all other European Commission initiatives were aimed at increasing competition and reducing the price of gas, but they did not square with the taxation policy.
"No incentive is according to the proposal created to increase its consumption," he said.
The proposals as they stand do, however, have one advantage, he said.

"If this proposal was to be put into force the tax advantage that coal enjoys in Germany...would be eliminated. An improvement in the competitive position of natural gas in relationship to coal is a particularly important factor when it comes to the prospects for natural gas in the generation of electricity," he said.
